workflows.name: Monitor EU EUDAMED recalls and MDR certificates with Apify, OpenAI and Slack

user.name: Francesco Pacifico
user.bio: Software engineer building HTTP-first Apify Actors & ready-to-run n8n automation pipelines for SecOps/TPRM vendor risk, KYB compliance, public procurement, EU healthcare, and judicial auctions.

workflows.description:
Quick overview
This workflow runs daily to monitor tracked EU EUDAMED UDI-DIs and manufacturer SRNs via Apify, keeps a stateful audit log in an n8n Data Table and Google Sheets, uses OpenAI to triage urgent compliance changes into CAPA guidance, and posts a consolidated alert brief to Slack.

How it works
Runs on a daily schedule (or manually in sample mode) and ensures the n8n Data Table used to store EUDAMED regulatory state exists.
Pulls device and expiring MDR certificate data from the Apify “EU EUDAMED Intelligence” actor based on your UDI-DI and SRN watchlists (or generates built-in sample records for testing).
Compares the latest Apify results with the stored state to detect new entities, recalls/FSCAs, conformity or risk changes, and certificate expiry countdown updates, then upserts the current state to the n8n Data Table.
Appends the detected changes to a Google Sheets tab as an audit ledger.
Selects only items that are new, changed, or due for an expiry reminder and sends up to five of the highest-priority items to OpenAI (gpt-4o-mini) to generate structured MDR/IVDR urgency, article references, impact summaries, and recommended QA actions.
Emails urgent items to a QA/RA address via Gmail and posts a grouped, consolidated regulatory brief to a Slack channel.
After Slack accepts the message, stamps the corresponding entities in the Data Table as notified/reminded, and if Apify or Slack fails it triggers an error workflow to post a failure alert to Slack.

Setup
Create an Apify token in Apify and add an n8n HTTP Header Auth credential that sets Authorization: Bearer , then select it in both Apify HTTP Request steps.
Add credentials for OpenAI, Google Sheets, Gmail, and Slack, and set the Slack channel where the brief and failure alerts should be posted.
Set your Google Sheets document ID and ensure a sheet/tab named EUDAMED_Audit exists for appending the audit log.
Update the watchlist and policy values (UDI-DIs, SRNs, expiry window, reminder days, QA email, and max items) in the configuration step, and optionally test using sampleDay 1 then sampleDay 2 before enabling live Apify calls.
In n8n workflow settings, set this workflow (or a dedicated one) as the error workflow so failures generate the Slack failure alert.

Requirements
n8n 2.48+ with Data Tables enabled (Cloud or self-hosted, core nodes only)
Apify account + API token (francescopacifico1905/eudamed-intelligence Pay-Per-Event)
OpenAI API key, Google Sheets, Gmail, and Slack workspace access

Customization
Adjust remindDaysBefore (90,30,7) or expiringWithinDays in Set UDI-DI Watchlist, SRNs & Alert Policy.
Customize CAPA scoring criteria in AI MDR/IVDR CAPA Triage or raise maxTotalChargeUsd on the Apify nodes for large hospital SKU catalogs.

Additional info
Uses synchronous Pay-Per-Event Apify calls capped at $0.25 per HTTP step; retry-on-fail is intentionally disabled to prevent double billing. Diagnostic NOT_FOUND / INVALID_IDENTIFIER items are never billed by the Actor.

workflows.name: Monitor incidents, health, and agent quality with OpenAI, Slack and Telegram

user.name: Vedant Pandya
user.bio: I build practical n8n workflows, AI agents, and intelligent automation systems for businesses. My focus is on reliable integrations, multi-agent orchestration, monitoring, and real-world productivity. Making powerful automation easier to deploy, understand, and maintain.

workflows.description:
Quick overview
Monitor n8n workflow failures, execution health, and AI agent quality from one workflow. OpenAI analyzes incidents and recommends corrective actions, while Slack and Telegram deliver configurable alerts. Includes scheduled health checks, agent evaluation, alert suppression, and optional incident logging for operational visibility.

How it works
This workflow combines three reliability-monitoring modules into a single n8n automation.
Incident Detection:* The Error Trigger receives execution failures from monitored n8n workflows. A manual demonstration trigger is also included for testing.
AI Incident Analysis:* Error information is normalized and sanitized before being sent to OpenAI. Two AI analysis stages classify the incident, identify possible causes, and recommend non-destructive troubleshooting steps.
Incident Alerts:* The workflow determines severity and applies a configurable alert cooldown to reduce repeated notifications. Incidents can be delivered to Slack and Telegram. Optional n8n Data Tables record incident details.
Scheduled Health Monitoring:* Every 15 minutes, the system retrieves recent executions and workflow information through the n8n API. It evaluates failure rates, execution duration, and configured critical-workflow inactivity.
Health Reporting:* Detected issues generate notifications. The workflow also supports daily health summaries and an optional external heartbeat integration.

Setup
Import the workflow:* Download the JSON file and import it into your n8n instance using the Import from File option.
Configure OpenAI:* Create an HTTP Bearer Auth credential using your OpenAI API key. Assign it to the AI Triage Analyst, AI Recovery Planner, and AI Quality Evaluator nodes. The default model is gpt-4.1-mini.
Connect Slack:* Create a Slack credential with permission to post messages to your selected channel. Assign it to the three Slack notification nodes.
Connect Telegram:* Create a Telegram bot using BotFather and obtain the destination chat ID. Configure the Telegram credentials on the three Telegram notification nodes.
Configure notification settings:* Open the Normalize Incident, Health Detector and Digest, and Normalize Agent Trace Code nodes. Update the notification channels, alert thresholds, and enable or disable optional integrations.
Configure n8n API access:* Create an n8n API credential and connect it to the Get Recent Executions and Get All Workflows nodes. The API credential must have permission to read execution and workflow information.
Optional audit logging:* Create the arc_incidents and arc_agent_evaluations Data Tables with the required columns. Select the correct tables in the audit nodes and enable Data Table logging in the configuration.
Secure the agent evaluation webhook:* Configure a Webhook Header Auth credential with an X-ARC-KEY header and a strong secret. Other agents can submit execution traces using this authenticated endpoint.
Test the workflow:* Run the manual demonstration triggers and verify the OpenAI responses, alert conditions, Slack messages, and Telegram notifications.
Enable monitoring:* Publish the combined workflow. Open each workflow you want to monitor, navigate to Settings, and select this workflow under Error Workflow.
Verify scheduled monitoring:* Confirm that the 15-minute health scanner executes correctly and that the n8n API returns execution data.
Complete all configuration and end-to-end tests before using the system in production.

Requirements
A compatible n8n instance with Error Trigger, Schedule Trigger, Webhook, Code, HTTP Request, and n8n API nodes.
An n8n API key with permission to read workflows and executions.
An OpenAI API key with access to gpt-4.1-mini for AI-powered analysis.
A Slack workspace and bot credential for Slack notifications (optional).
A Telegram bot token and destination chat ID for Telegram notifications (optional).
n8n Data Tables for persistent incident and evaluation records (optional).
An external heartbeat monitoring service such as Healthchecks.io (optional).
An authenticated webhook credential for receiving agent evaluation traces.
Appropriate permissions to configure an Error Workflow on monitored automations.
External services may have separate usage charges. Credentials are not included in the downloadable JSON.

Customization
The workflow is designed to be customized for different n8n environments and operational requirements.
Alert channels:** Enable or disable Slack and Telegram independently and configure destination channels or chat IDs.
AI model:** Change the OpenAI model in the HTTP Request nodes to a compatible model available to your API account.
Monitoring frequency:** Adjust the default 15-minute schedule according to your operational requirements.
Failure thresholds:** Customize failure-rate, execution-duration, and critical-workflow inactivity thresholds.
Alert suppression:** Adjust notification cooldown periods to reduce repeated incident alerts.
Critical workflows:** Specify important workflow IDs and their maximum expected inactivity periods.
Agent evaluation:** Adjust quality scoring and operational thresholds for response time, tool usage, and estimated costs.
Audit logging:** Enable optional Data Tables for incident history and agent evaluation records.
External monitoring:** Configure an optional heartbeat endpoint to help detect missed monitoring runs.
Manual testing:** Use the included demonstration triggers to validate the monitoring branches before production use.
For high-volume environments, extend execution pagination, persistent alert suppression, and monitoring infrastructure as required.

Additional info
Agent Reliability Center (ARC) — AI-Assisted Monitoring Template

This template combines incident triage, execution health monitoring, and AI agent quality evaluation into one workflow with independent triggers.

Primary use cases:
Monitoring business-critical n8n automations
Investigating failed executions
Detecting increased workflow failure rates
Reviewing AI agent output and tool usage
Monitoring reported latency and estimated token costs
Sending operational alerts to Slack and Telegram
Maintaining optional incident audit records

Security and operational considerations:

AI-generated diagnoses are recommendations, not verified root-cause findings. The workflow does not automatically retry failed business operations, change credentials, delete records, or perform destructive recovery actions.

Agent evaluation depends on the trace information supplied by the calling application. Token counts and estimated costs are not independently verified against provider billing data.

Notification cooldowns use best-effort workflow state and are not designed to guarantee exactly-once delivery across distributed installations.

Testing status: The workflow JSON has undergone offline structural and syntax validation. Each user must configure credentials and complete live integration testing before relying on it in production.

This is an extensible monitoring starter system rather than a replacement for a dedicated enterprise observability platform.

workflows.name: Monitor company news and log business events with Anthropic and Google Sheets

user.name: Owlab
user.bio: Owlab builds AI agents, voice agents first, plus AI automation and AI products. We build n8n workflows for complex business processes and AI-powered integrations with the systems you already use. We've built software since 2012: an Estonian company with a team in Ukraine and the EU.

workflows.description:
Quick overview
This workflow runs on a schedule to monitor Google News RSS results for a list of companies, uses Anthropic to classify headlines into business event types, and appends deduplicated events to a Google Sheets tab.

How it works
Runs every morning on a schedule (or manually) and loads the monitoring settings, including the company list, lookback window, and Google Sheets target.
Builds one Google News RSS search URL per company and fetches matching headlines from Google News.
Filters results to recent items where the company name appears in the headline, limits the number of headlines per company, and skips links already checked in previous executions.
Sends each headline and snippet to Anthropic to extract whether it is about the company plus an event type, event date, people involved, and a verbatim quote.
Combines the AI output with the source headline data, drops passing mentions, and generates an event key to group duplicate reports.
Removes items classified as “other”, deduplicates multiple outlets reporting the same event, skips events already logged in previous executions, and appends the remaining events to Google Sheets.

Setup
Add an Anthropic API credential for the chat model used by the information extraction step (or replace it with another compatible LLM node).
Add a Google Sheets OAuth2 credential and update the spreadsheet URL and sheet/tab name in the monitoring settings.
Create the target tab in the spreadsheet (or ensure the named sheet exists) and edit the company list, keywords, locale, and limits in the monitoring settings before activating the workflow.

Requirements
n8n with the AI (LangChain) nodes. Built and tested on n8n 2.21, self-hosted.
A Google account with access to Google Sheets.
An Anthropic API key, or a key for another chat model provider. Each headline is one short model call.

Customization
Event types: edit the rules in the system prompt and the enum in the schema of Classify business event, then update the list at the top of Combine AI result with headline.
Search scope: edit eventKeywords to widen or narrow the results, or leave it empty to check all news about each company.
Region and language: change newsLanguage (for example de) and newsCountry (for example DE).
Destination: the rows that reach the last node are flat, so you can replace Append events to Google Sheets with an Airtable, Baserow, Notion or database node. Use event_key as the unique key if you upsert.
Alerts: add a Slack or email node after the last node to get a message for each new event.

Additional info
Limitations: the AI reads only headlines and short snippets, not full articles, so event_date is often empty. Google News links are Google redirect URLs. The Google News RSS feed is meant for personal feed readers, so check its terms for your use case or swap in a news API. Duplicate checks use the n8n deduplication store: to process the same headlines again, run the Remove Duplicates nodes once with the operation Clear Deduplication History.

workflows.name: Monitor WhatsApp template health with OpenAI, Gmail and Slack alerts
workflows.description:
Quick overview
This workflow runs daily to check WhatsApp Cloud API phone number health and message template status via the Meta Graph API, compares results with the previous run, optionally generates OpenAI rewrite suggestions for newly rejected templates, and sends severity-based alerts via Gmail (and optional Slack) with Google Sheets logging.

How it works
Runs every morning at 8:00 (or manually) and loads your WhatsApp Business Account, phone number IDs, and alert settings.
Calls the Meta Graph API to fetch health details for each configured phone number (quality rating, status, messaging limit tier, and display name status) and lists all message templates in the account with pagination.
Consolidates the results into a single “health snapshot,” turning any Graph API failures into actionable issues with suggested fixes.
Compares the snapshot to the previous baseline stored in workflow static data so only new issues, resolved issues, and messaging-limit tier changes are reported (or sends a daily summary if enabled).
For newly rejected templates (when enabled), uses an OpenAI chat model to read the template details from the Meta Graph API and attach a suggested BODY rewrite and category adjustment to the report.
Builds an HTML alert, optionally posts critical alerts to Slack, sends the full alert email via Gmail, then saves the current snapshot as the next baseline and optionally appends Errors and Health log rows to Google Sheets.

Setup
Create a WhatsApp Cloud API (Meta Graph API) credential using a permanent System User access token with whatsapp_business_management permission and access to your WhatsApp Business Account.
Add a Gmail credential for sending alert emails and set the recipient address in the workflow settings.
Add an OpenAI credential (used for rejected-template rewrite suggestions) and disable AI suggestions if you don’t want OpenAI involved.
In “Set Health Check Settings,” replace the YOUR_ placeholders (waba_id, phone_number_ids, alert_email, and optional sheet_url) and optionally set watched_templates, slack_alerts/slack_channel, and the logging toggles.
If Google Sheets logging is enabled, provide a Google Sheets credential and ensure the target spreadsheet contains the specified tab names (for example, “Errors” and “Health log”).
If Slack alerts are enabled, add a Slack credential and ensure the configured channel (for example, #whatsapp-alerts) exists.

workflows.name: Monitor new USPTO trademarks with Apify and send alerts to Sheets and Slack

user.name: Magnova
user.bio: Magnova builds production-ready Apify Actors and plug-and-play n8n workflows that turn public web sources into clean, structured data. Simple pay-per-event pricing with no start fees—ready to connect straight to Google Sheets, Slack, and AI pipelines. Browse all our Actors & video tutorials via the link below.

workflows.description:
Quick overview
This workflow runs daily to search recent USPTO trademark filings via Apify for a given wordmark, then logs newly seen matches to Google Sheets and posts alerts to Slack, while suppressing notifications on the first run by establishing a baseline of previously found serial numbers.

How it works
Runs every day on a schedule trigger.
Sets the target brand keyword and calculates a “filed after” date for the last 90 days.
Uses Apify to run the USPTO Trademark Search actor and return live trademark filings matching the keyword.
Compares each result’s serial number against stored history to keep only filings that have not been seen before, and on the first run returns a baseline message instead of alerts.
If it is the baseline run, posts a “baseline established” message to a Slack channel.
Otherwise, appends each new filing to Google Sheets and posts a formatted Slack alert with the TSDR link to the official USPTO record.

Setup
Add an Apify API token credential and ensure the workflow can run the USPTO Trademark Search actor (ID: I8KvtBliDeyVghVzU).
Update the monitored keyword by replacing YOUR BRAND in the brand setting.
Connect your Google Sheets account, set the target spreadsheet URL/ID, and create a sheet with headers: Wordmark, Owner, Status, Filed, Serial number, Registration number, TSDR link.
Connect your Slack account and set the alert channel (for example, #trademark-alerts) for both Slack messages.
Run the workflow once to establish the baseline, then activate it for ongoing daily monitoring.

workflows.name: Monitor domain expiry, SSL and email security with Apify and Google Sheets
workflows.description:
Quick overview
This workflow runs every Monday to check a list of domains using Apify Domain Intelligence, then writes registrar, domain and SSL expiry, email security (SPF/DMARC), and website status into Google Sheets with an Issues column that flags problems.

How it works
Runs every Monday at 08:00 on a schedule.
Sends the configured domain list to Apify Domain Intelligence and retrieves DNS, SSL, email, and website status details.
Keeps only results that are valid domain reports and ignores non-domain/error rows.
Builds a per-domain Issues summary (expiry warnings, SSL trust/expiry, SPF/DMARC gaps, and website errors) and formats the remaining fields for reporting.
Appends new rows or updates existing rows in Google Sheets by matching on the Domain column.

Setup
Create an Apify account, generate an API token, and add an HTTP Header Auth credential that sets Authorization: Bearer  for the Apify request.
Update the domain list and warnDays threshold in the workflow to control what gets checked and when expiry warnings appear.
Connect Google Sheets, paste your spreadsheet URL and pick the tab. The first row needs these headers: Domain, Issues, Registrar, Domain expires, Days to expiry, SSL expires, SSL days left, Email provider, SPF, DMARC policy, HTTP status, Final URL, Last checked. After picking the tab, n8n resets the mapping: set Mapping Column Mode back to Map Automatically and Column to match on to “Domain”.

Requirements
An Apify account (the free plan's monthly credit covers small lists; the Domain Intelligence Actor costs about $5 per 1,000 domain checks) and a Google account with Google Sheets.

Customization
Change warnDays, run daily instead of weekly, or add a Filter on Issues != "OK" followed by Slack, Gmail or Microsoft Teams to get alerted only when something needs attention.

Additional info
Registration data comes from RDAP, the official successor to WHOIS; some country domains (for example .io and .es) don't publish it, so their registrar and expiry stay empty. DMARC is only flagged for domains that receive email. One run must finish within 5 minutes, which covers a few hundred domains. Tested on n8n 2.46.6. Disclosure: I built the Apify Actor this template uses.

user.name: Hanna Nosova

workflows.description:
Catch regressions, security reports and breaking changes in the open-source libraries you depend on before they reach your users. Each weekday this template fetches new and updated issues from the GitHub repositories you list, using the FetchCat GitHub Issues & Pull Requests Scraper on Apify. No GitHub login is needed. One OpenAI call scores each issue for upgrade and production risk, every issue is logged to Google Sheets, and only the high-risk ones are posted to Slack.

How it works

A manual run or a weekday schedule (9:00) reads your repositories, lookback window and limits from one settings node.
The Apify node runs fetch_cat/github-issues-pull-requests-scraper once per repository and returns the issues updated in the last 7 days, most recent first. One failed repository is reported and the others continue.
Issues already in your Google Sheet with no new activity are skipped, so nothing is scored twice.
One gpt-5.4-mini call with a strict JSON schema returns, for each issue, a category (bug, regression, security, breaking change, feature or question), a risk score from 1 to 5, whether it affects upgrades and a one-line summary. The answer is validated before anything is written.
Google Sheets gets one row per issue (matched on URL). Issues at risk 4 or higher go to one Slack digest, once each. A quiet day posts nothing.

Setup

Make a copy of the sheet template.
Add the Apify node (verified node on n8n Cloud, @apify/n8n-nodes-apify on self-hosted) and connect your Apify account.
Connect OpenAI, Google Sheets (pick your copy in both Sheets nodes) and Slack (pick a channel).
List your dependencies in 1. Set your watched repositories and run once by hand. Publish the workflow to turn on the weekday schedule.

Setup takes about 10 minutes. A default run (3 repositories, up to 10 issues each) costs about USD 0.02 on Apify plus one small OpenAI call, and maxCostUsdPerRepository caps each Apify run.

Requirements

n8n 2.47.4 or newer with the Apify node
Apify account
OpenAI API key
Google Sheets and Slack accounts

Customization

Change the repositories, lookback window, state, labels and limits in the settings node.
Raise alertMinRiskScore to 5 for only the most severe items, or set includePullRequests to true to score fix pull requests too.
Swap Slack for Teams, Discord or email: the digest is one item with a text field.
Scores use the title, labels, comment and reaction counts and the first part of the issue body, not the full thread, so read the issue before acting.

workflows.name: Monitor self-hosted n8n uptime and workflow failures with Vivere
workflows.description:
Quick overview
Get alerted when your self-hosted n8n instance goes down, stops running schedules, or workflows fail. Every 5 minutes this workflow checks the n8n API for failed executions and pings a Vivere heartbeat monitor. If the instance stops, the pings stop, and Vivere alerts you from outside n8n.

How it works
Runs every 5 minutes on a schedule.
Reads up to 100 recent n8n executions with status "error" using the n8n API.
Filters failures to only those within the configured look-back window and ignores failures from this watchdog workflow itself, or captures an API error if the n8n API call fails.
Sends a success ping to your Vivere heartbeat monitor when no recent failures are found.
When failures are found, fetches workflow names from the n8n API and builds a short text summary mapping workflow IDs to names.
Sends a fail ping to Vivere containing the failure summary, or sends a fail ping describing the API error when the n8n API is unreachable or misconfigured.

Setup
Create an n8n API key (Settings → n8n API) and add an n8n API credential with your instance base URL ending in /api/v1.
Sign up at vivere.dev, create a Heartbeat monitor with a 5-minute period and a 5-minute grace, and copy its ping URL.
Paste the Vivere ping URL into the workflow configuration and adjust lookbackMinutes (and the schedule interval) to match your desired check frequency.

Requirements
A self-hosted n8n instance with the public API enabled, and a free Vivere account (25 monitors, email and webhook alerts, 5-minute minimum period).

Customization
Check less often by changing the trigger, lookbackMinutes and the monitor's period together, or ignore noisy workflows by filtering their ids out in Check executions.

Additional info
Why check from outside: an error workflow or an in-n8n watchdog runs inside the instance it watches, so it can't alert you when that instance is down, a restart didn't come back, or the scheduler stalled. Here the missing ping is the alert. More on catching n8n workflows that stopped silently: https://vivere.dev/answers/n8n-workflows-stopped-no-alert?utm_source=n8n-template&utm_campaign=22556

workflows.name: Monitor workflow health with n8n executions, data tables and Slack alerts

user.name: Ashley Gross
user.bio: Founder and CEO of The Alliance, an enterprise AI advisory and implementation firm. I build n8n workflows that connect CRMs, meetings, analytics, and AI agents into one system, with monitoring that catches failures before your clients do. Wiley-published author of The AI Workweek. 2,500+ professionals trained at Fortune 500 companies. Use my link to book a call for custom n8n work.

workflows.description:
Quick overview
Catch workflows that run green but do nothing. List each workflow once in a Data Table, and this monitor checks its executions hourly. It flags missing runs, errors, stale successes, and empty output, then sends one Slack digest. No changes to the workflows you watch.

How it works
Runs every hour on a schedule (or on manual trigger).
Loads all rows from an n8n Data Table and keeps only the expectations marked as enabled.
For each enabled workflow, uses the n8n API to fetch its 10 most recent executions.
Evaluates each workflow for never ran, latest run error, no recent success within the allowed time window, and too few items produced by the specified check node.
Updates the corresponding Data Table row with the latest check time, status, and item count from the most recent successful run.
Aggregates all results and, if any workflows have issues, posts a single digest message to a Slack channel.

Setup
Create an n8n API key and add an n8n API credential (Base URL must include /api/v1) for reading executions.
Create and select an n8n Data Table containing columns like workflow_id, workflow_name, check_node, min_items, max_hours, enabled, last_status, last_checked, and last_items, then add one row per workflow to monitor.
Ensure the monitored workflows save successful executions and that check_node matches the target node name exactly.
Add a Slack credential and set the destination channel (for example #automation-alerts).

Requirements
n8n API key (Settings > n8n API) with access to executions
An n8n plan with Data Tables (n8n Cloud or a recent self-hosted version)
Slack workspace and credential (or swap in Gmail, Teams, or Discord)
Monitored workflows set to save successful production executions

Customization
Change the schedule to every 15 minutes for critical workflows, or daily for low-volume ones
Point check_node at the last node that writes or sends something, like a CRM write or email send
Swap SendSlackAlert for Gmail, Microsoft Teams, or Discord
Use the Data Table as a health dashboard: last_status, last_checked, and last_items update on every run

Additional info
Limitations: it reads the last 10 executions per workflow, so execution pruning limits how far back it can see. A node on an untaken IF branch doesn't appear in execution data, so it counts as 0 items (this is intentional, and how empty branches get caught). Alerts repeat each hour until the problem clears. Tested on n8n Cloud in November 2026 against four failure cases (errored, stale, missing, and empty output) plus three healthy workflows.

Quick overview
This workflow monitors selected n8n workflows via the n8n public API to detect “silent failures” such as empty successful runs, missed schedules, switched-off workflows, and missing expected records, then sends alerts to Slack and email and logs findings to Google Sheets.

How it works
Runs every 15 minutes to check watched workflows, sends a daily Slack summary at 8am, and also supports a manual test run with sample data.
Reads your monitoring configuration, including the n8n base URL and a JSON list of workflows to check and their thresholds.
For each configured workflow, calls the n8n API to fetch the workflow status (active/inactive) and its recent executions, and optionally calls a separate “record check” URL to count expected records.
Evaluates recent executions to flag empty successful runs (too few items past a specified step), missed schedules (no execution within the allowed gap), inactive workflows, missing records at the check URL, and optionally failed runs.
Deduplicates findings so each unique problem is only reported once, while also tracking check activity for the daily summary.
Sends a bundled alert to Slack and an email with links to the affected workflows/executions, and appends each finding as a new row in a Google Sheets log.

Enable the n8n public API, create an n8n API key, and add an HTTP Header Auth credential (for example X-N8N-API-KEY) for the n8n API requests.
Update the Config values, especially n8n_base_url, slack_webhook_url, alert_email, from_email, lookback_hours, and checks_json with your real workflow IDs, node names to count, and schedule/record thresholds.
Create a Slack incoming webhook and add its URL to the Config.
Configure an SMTP email credential for the email alert step.
Connect Google Sheets OAuth credentials, set the target spreadsheet ID, and ensure it has a tab named “Silent failures” for appending log rows.

workflows.description:
Quick Overview
This workflow monitors selected PyPI packages by running an Apify actor to collect release and download activity, scores each update with OpenAI, stores results in Google Sheets, and sends Slack approval alerts for high-priority items plus Gmail digests and a weekly email report.

How it works
Runs on a daily schedule (or manually), and also runs a separate weekly schedule to produce a 7-day report.
On daily runs, starts an Apify actor run to fetch PyPI package release and download stats, then waits and polls the Apify API until the run succeeds or fails.
Downloads the Apify dataset results, removes invalid entries, and deduplicates already-seen package/version pairs using persisted workflow memory.
Calculates a rule-based activity score per package and uses OpenAI (via an LLM chain with structured JSON output) to produce a fit score, verdict, summary, and red flags, then blends rule and AI scores into a final tier.
Upserts each scored record into Google Sheets keyed by package@version, then routes hot items to Slack for approve/dismiss review, warm items to a Gmail HTML digest, and keeps cold items in the sheet only.
For hot Slack reviews, writes the approval decision back to Google Sheets, and on the weekly schedule, reads the sheet to email a 7-day summary report via Gmail.
If any execution fails, formats the error details and posts an alert message to a Slack channel.

Setup
Add an Apify API token as an HTTP Header Auth credential (Authorization: Bearer ) and select it on the Apify HTTP Request nodes.
Connect your OpenAI credential (or replace the chat model node with another provider) and keep the model selection updated.
Connect Google Sheets OAuth credentials, create a sheet tab with the expected columns, and set the Google Sheet ID and tab name in the Config node.
Connect Slack OAuth credentials, set the Slack channel ID in Config (and in the error-alert Slack node), and ensure the channel allows interactive approve/dismiss messages.

workflows.name: Monitor Reddit and score leads with Apify, OpenAI, OpenRouter and Slack
workflows.description:
Quick overview
This workflow monitors Reddit hourly via Apify, filters and scores new posts (with OpenAI/OpenRouter or keyword rules), logs them to an n8n Data Table (optionally Google Sheets), sends high-relevance alerts to Slack, and posts a daily 24-hour digest to Slack every morning.

How it works
Runs on a schedule every hour to fetch newly published Reddit posts from configured subreddits and keyword searches using Apify.
Cleans the results by excluding NSFW content, blocked words, low-score posts, and (optionally) search hits that don’t strictly match your keywords.
Skips posts that have already been processed in previous executions.
Scores each post for relevance and intent and generates a short summary and suggested reply using OpenAI/OpenRouter (or applies a keyword-based scoring fallback when AI is disabled).
Logs each scored post to an n8n Data Table and optionally appends the same data to a Google Sheets tab.
Sends an immediate Slack alert for posts whose relevance meets or exceeds the configured alert threshold.
Runs every morning to compile the last 24 hours of logged posts, optionally uses OpenAI/OpenRouter to write a brief Slack-formatted briefing, and posts the digest to Slack.

Setup
Add an Apify API token credential and ensure the Apify actor run limit (maxSpendUsdPerRun) matches your budget.
Add a Slack OAuth credential, invite the bot to your target channel, and set the channel in both Slack messages (alert and digest).
Add an OpenAI credential (or an OpenRouter key via the same credential by setting the Base URL to https://openrouter.ai/api/v1) if useAI is enabled.
Update the Config values for subreddits, keywords, excluded words, and your “about you” description, plus thresholds like alertScore and digestTopN.
(Optional) Enable the Google Sheets step, connect Google Sheets OAuth, and replace the placeholder document URL and sheet name to log posts to a spreadsheet.

workflows.name: Monitor SPF, DKIM and DMARC across multiple domains with Apify, Gmail and Slack
workflows.description:
Quick overview
This workflow runs daily (or on demand) to audit SPF, DKIM, and DMARC for multiple domains using the Apify Email Deliverability Auditor, tracks changes in an n8n Data Table ledger, and notifies results via Gmail digest emails and Slack messages for new, changed, or fixed findings.

How it works
Runs on a daily schedule at 7:00 or is started manually, then loads domain, DKIM selector, and notification settings from a configuration block.
Ensures a deliverability_ledger n8n Data Table exists and splits the configured domain list into one item per domain.
Calls the Apify Email Deliverability Auditor Actor for each domain to check SPF, DKIM, and DMARC, retrying once after 30 seconds if the audit fails.
Converts each audit result into per-check findings (critical, warning, info, or ok), including a recorded DNS/audit failure finding when both attempts fail.
Compares the current findings to the Data Table ledger to label each check as new, changed, still open, fixed, or ok, then upserts the latest state back to the ledger.
Builds an HTML digest and a Slack change summary, then sends the digest via Gmail every run and posts to Slack only when there are changes.

Setup
Add an Apify HTTP Header Auth credential with an Authorization header set to Bearer .
Connect Gmail credentials for sending the digest email and Slack credentials for posting messages (or disable either channel in the configuration).
Update the CONFIG block with your domains, DKIM selectors, notification email address, and Slack channel name.
Ensure your n8n instance supports Data Tables and that it can create/use a table named deliverability_ledger.

Requirements
n8n with Data Tables (tested on 2.43), an Apify account (Email Deliverability Auditor Actor), Gmail and/or Slack.

Customization
Tune spfLookupWarningAt, dmarcTargetPolicy, softfailIsInfo and requireDkim in CONFIG. About $0.002 per domain per check on Apify.

Additional info
Disclosure: the Apify Actor used here was built and is published by the author of this template (EdenWorks). You pay Apify's usage price when it runs and the author earns part of that fee. Apify's free plan credits cover light use.

workflows.name: Monitor Google Maps listing changes with Apify, OpenAI, Sheets, Slack, and Gmail
workflows.description:
Quick Overview
This workflow runs daily to monitor Google Maps listing changes via an Apify actor, scores each change with OpenAI and rules, logs results to Google Sheets, and routes hot items to Slack for approval and warm items to a Gmail digest, with a separate weekly email report.

How it works
Runs on a daily schedule (or manually), and on Mondays runs a weekly-report-only schedule.
For daily runs, starts the Apify Google Maps listing change monitor actor, then waits and polls the Apify run status until it succeeds or fails.
Downloads the Apify dataset results, validates required fields, and deduplicates records against prior runs using workflow static data.
Scores each change with a rule-based urgency score and then uses OpenAI to produce a structured fit score, verdict, summary, outreach angle, and red flags, combining both into a final tier.
Upserts all scored rows into a Google Sheets tab keyed by a unique record key to avoid duplicates across reruns.
Sends hot-tier items as a single Slack approval message (approve/dismiss) and writes the review decision back to the same Google Sheets rows.
Sends warm-tier items as an HTML email digest via Gmail, while cold-tier items remain stored in Google Sheets only.
For weekly runs, reads the last 7 days of rows from Google Sheets, builds a top-items summary, and emails the weekly report via Gmail, and on any workflow failure posts an error alert to Slack.

Setup
Add an Apify API token as an HTTP Header Auth credential (Authorization: Bearer ) and select it on the Apify HTTP Request steps.
Connect Google Sheets credentials, create a spreadsheet tab for the listing-change log, and set the Google Sheet ID and tab name in the Config values.
Connect an OpenAI credential (or replace the chat model node with another provider) and ensure the workflow can return structured JSON output for the verdict fields.
Connect Slack credentials, set the target Slack channel ID for approvals (and the separate error-alert channel ID if different), and ensure interactive approvals are enabled for send-and-wait.
Connect Gmail credentials and set the digestEmail address in Config to receive the warm daily digest and weekly report.
Update the Apify actor input in Config (searches, max places, alertOn events, thresholds, and monitorKey) and adjust scoring thresholds (hotScore/warmScore) and AI criteria as needed.

workflows.name: Monitor AI agent runs with Gemini judge, Google Sheets, Slack and Gmail

user.name: Ali Abdullah
user.bio: AI Engineer (FDE) & AI Automation Expert. I build autonomous agents, RAG pipelines, and workflow automations that run in production, not demos. Verified n8n Creator. I take AI from pilot to deployed across live business operations. No slideware, only shipped systems.

workflows.description:
Quick overview
This live watchdog monitors AI agent executions daily, sampling runs for Gemini judge scoring, tracking quality drift, and detecting cost, latency, and silent-failure anomalies. It logs scores and baselines to Google Sheets and alerts operations via Slack, Telegram, and Gmail.

How it works
Runs on a daily schedule (or manually) and loads configuration values such as the monitored n8n URL, API key, workflow IDs, sampling settings, and alert thresholds.
Validates the configuration and builds an n8n executions API request for the lookback window, then fetches recent executions from the monitored n8n instance.
If the executions fetch fails, sends a Gmail alert to the ops email address and stops the run gracefully.
Normalizes execution records, estimates cost from token counts, deduplicates against previously scored execution IDs stored in Google Sheets, and flags failed runs and “silent failures” (for example, empty or error-like output despite a success status).
Always selects failures and silent failures for review and deterministically samples additional runs, then uses Google Gemini to judge the sampled outputs and produce a 0–100 score with a short reason.
Compares current window metrics (mean score, cost, mean/p95 latency, silent-failure rate) against pooled historical baselines from Google Sheets to detect drift and threshold breaches, with an alert cooldown based on recent alert history.
Appends per-run scores and a baseline snapshot to Google Sheets, posts alerts to Slack (and Telegram if enabled), logs alert decisions to Google Sheets, and sends a daily digest email via Gmail.

Setup
Create an n8n API key on the monitored instance and set the correct n8nBaseUrl, n8nApiKey, lookbackHours, and workflow ID filters (or clear targetWorkflowIds to watch all) in the configuration.
Create a Google Sheet with tabs named RunScores, Baselines, and AlertLog, add a Google Sheets credential in n8n, and set sheetId in the configuration.
Add credentials for Gmail and Slack, then set opsEmail and slackChannelId (and enableTelegram plus telegramChatId and Telegram credentials if you want Telegram alerts).
Add a Google Gemini API key, set the geminiModel if needed, and tune sampling/threshold settings (sampleRate, maxJudgePerRun, driftStdDev, score/cost/latency floors, alertCooldownHours, and token prices) before activating the workflow.
